questions.question: Write a note on factors affecting the jelly preparation.
questions.solution_html:
• Jelly preparation depends on the quality of fruit juice, pectin concentration, sugar content, acidity
  • and cooking conditions. Fruits should contain sufficient pectin and suitable natural acids for
  • proper gel formation. Sugar contributes to sweetness and helps establish the conditions required
  • for gel formation. The pectin concentration influences the firmness of the jelly, while acidity
  • affects the strength and formation of the gel network. Cooking should be controlled to achieve
  • the correct concentration without excessive heating, which may damage pectin or affect flavour
  • and colour. Proper straining, filling and sealing are also important for producing a clear, firm and
  • stable jelly.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: List the major pigments present in fruits and vegetables and state their characteristic colours.
questions.solution_html:
• List the major pigments present in fruits and vegetables and state their characteristic colours.
  • The major pigments in fruits and vegetables include chlorophylls, carotenoids, anthocyanins
  • betalains and flavonoids. Chlorophylls produce green colours and are found in leafy vegetables
  • such as spinach. Carotenoids produce yellow, orange and red colours; examples include beta
  • carotene in carrots and lycopene in tomatoes. Anthocyanins produce red, purple and blue colours
  • in fruits such as grapes, berries and plums. Betalains provide red-violet and yellow colours and
  • are particularly characteristic of beetroot. Flavonoids, including certain flavones and flavonols
  • contribute pale yellow colours and other aspects of plant appearance. These pigments influence
  • the colour, attractiveness and perceived quality of fruits and vegetables.
questions.final_answer: the colour, attractiveness and perceived quality of fruits and vegetables
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain simultaneous heat transfer and mass transfer during drying.
questions.solution_html:
• Drying involves simultaneous heat transfer and mass transfer. Heat is supplied to the food by hot
  • air, a heated surface or another energy source. This heat raises the temperature of the material
  • and provides the energy needed to evaporate moisture. At the same time, water moves from the
  • interior of the food towards the surface, where it evaporates into the surrounding air. The water
  • vapour is then carried away by the drying medium. The rate of drying depends on temperature
  • air velocity, relative humidity, surface area, food thickness and the initial moisture content.
  • Proper control of these factors helps achieve efficient drying while limiting undesirable changes
  • in colour, flavour, texture and nutritional quality.
questions.final_answer: in colour, flavour, texture and nutritional quality
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain fermented beverage and classify them with suitable examples
questions.solution_html:
• Fermented beverages are drinks produced when microorganisms convert sugars or other
  • fermentable substances into alcohol, organic acids and other products. Alcoholic fermented
  • beverages include wine, produced mainly by the fermentation of grape or other fruit sugars, and
  • cider, produced from fermented apple juice. Beer is produced by fermenting a prepared cereal
  • based wort, usually made from malted grains. Non-alcoholic or low-alcohol fermented beverages
  • include products such as kombucha and certain traditional cereal-based beverages, depending on
  • their preparation and final alcohol content. Fermentation develops characteristic flavours and
  • aromas and may improve product keeping quality. The type of raw material, microorganisms
  • fermentation conditions and processing method determine the characteristics of the final
  • beverage.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the different methods used in cleaning of fruits and vegetables.
questions.solution_html:
• Cleaning fruits and vegetables removes soil, dust, plant debris, insects and surface contaminants
  • before further processing. Dry cleaning methods include brushing, wiping, screening and air
  • cleaning, which are suitable for removing loose dirt from appropriate produce. Wet cleaning
  • involves washing with potable water through immersion, spraying or water-flume systems.
  • Mechanical agitation may improve the removal of adhering dirt, provided it does not damage
  • delicate produce. Sanitizing treatments, such as approved chlorine-based solutions or other
  • permitted sanitizers, may be used under controlled conditions to reduce surface microorganisms.
  • Electrolyzed water and ozone may also be used in suitable processing systems. The method
  • selected depends on the type of produce, contamination level and sensitivity to physical damage.
  • Proper drainage and hygienic handling after washing are necessary to prevent recontamination.
questions.final_answer: Proper drainage and hygienic handling after washing are necessary to prevent recontamination
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the principles and applications of controlled atmosphere packaging and modified atmosphere packaging in fresh produce storage.
questions.solution_html:
• atmosphere packaging in fresh produce storage.
  • Modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) and controlled atmosphere storage (CA) are techniques
  • used to extend the storage life of fresh fruits and vegetables by modifying the gaseous
  • environment around the produce. In MAP, the atmosphere inside a package is modified through
  • gas flushing, suitable packaging materials and the interaction between produce respiration and
  • gas transmission through the film. Oxygen is generally reduced and carbon dioxide is adjusted to
  • levels suitable for the particular commodity. This slows respiration and may delay ripening
  • senescence and microbial deterioration. The composition of the atmosphere can change during
  • storage.
  • In controlled atmosphere storage, oxygen, carbon dioxide, temperature and humidity are
  • monitored and adjusted to maintain specified conditions throughout storage. This method is
  • commonly used for the long-term storage of suitable fruits, particularly apples. Both methods
  • require commodity-specific conditions because excessively low oxygen or excessively high
  • carbon dioxide can cause off-flavours, fermentation or physiological injury.
  • Applications include the storage and distribution of apples, grapes, berries, fresh-cut vegetables
  • and salad products. These technologies reduce quality deterioration, help maintain firmness and
  • freshness, and can reduce post-harvest losses. Their success depends on selecting suitable gas
  • concentrations, packaging materials, storage temperatures and handling practices. MAP and CA
  • do not replace hygiene, refrigeration or other necessary food safety measures.
questions.final_answer: do not replace hygiene, refrigeration or other necessary food safety measures
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Classify the major freezing methods based on mode of heat transfer and present suitable applications for each method.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify the major freezing methods based on mode of heat transfer and present suitable
  • applications for each method.
  • Freezing preserves fruits and vegetables by lowering their temperature sufficiently to convert a
  • substantial proportion of their water into ice. It slows microbial growth and many chemical and
  • enzymatic reactions. Freezing methods can be classified according to the way heat is removed
  • from the product.
  • Air-blast freezing uses rapidly circulating cold air to remove heat from food. It is suitable for
  • fruits, vegetables and other products, especially when a flexible system is required. Fluidized
  • bed freezing is a form of air freezing in which small individual pieces, such as peas and diced
  • vegetables, are suspended by a stream of cold air, allowing rapid and relatively uniform freezing.
  • Contact or plate freezing transfers heat through direct contact between packaged food and
  • refrigerated metal plates. It is suitable for flat packages and products of uniform thickness.
  • Immersion freezing involves placing suitable food or packages in a cold liquid medium, allowing
  • rapid heat transfer; the medium must be appropriate for the product and packaging.
  • Cryogenic freezing uses very cold substances such as liquid nitrogen or carbon dioxide to freeze
  • food rapidly. It is useful for high-value products, delicate fruits and individually quick-frozen
  • items, although operating costs may be high.
  • The choice of method depends on product size, shape, packaging, required freezing rate, cost and
  • final quality. Rapid freezing generally produces smaller ice crystals and can reduce tissue
  • damage and drip loss during thawing. Correct packaging and stable frozen storage are necessary
  • to maintain quality.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the methods used to control post-harvest losses.
questions.solution_html:
• Post-harvest losses can be controlled through careful harvesting, suitable handling, proper
  • storage, effective transportation and appropriate processing. Fruits and vegetables should be
  • harvested at the correct maturity stage using methods that minimize bruising, cuts and crushing.
  • Sorting and grading remove damaged, diseased and unsuitable produce and help maintain
  • uniform quality.
  • Pre-cooling after harvest removes field heat and slows respiration and deterioration. Refrigerated
  • storage at the appropriate temperature and relative humidity reduces moisture loss and delays
  • ripening. However, chilling-sensitive commodities must be stored within their recommended
  • temperature range. Suitable packaging protects produce from mechanical damage and reduces
  • moisture loss. Refrigerated or well-managed transportation helps maintain the cold chain and
  • prevents rapid quality deterioration.
  • Other methods include controlled atmosphere storage, modified atmosphere packaging and
  • edible coatings, which can help slow respiration and moisture loss when properly applied.
  • Sanitation, pest control and hygienic handling reduce microbial spoilage. Processing methods
  • such as canning, freezing, drying, fermentation and preparation of jams and juices convert
  • surplus or perishable produce into more stable products. Training handlers, improving storage
  • infrastructure and maintaining accurate stock rotation further reduce losses. An integrated
  • approach is most effective because post-harvest deterioration can occur at every stage between
  • harvesting and consumption.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discusss the factors affecting vinegar production, including temperature,acidity,oxygen supply and microbial activity
questions.solution_html:
• supply and microbial activity.
  • Vinegar is produced mainly through the conversion of ethanol into acetic acid by acetic acid
  • bacteria under aerobic conditions. The process generally involves two stages: alcoholic
  • fermentation, in which yeast converts sugars into ethanol, followed by acetic acid fermentation
  • in which suitable bacteria convert ethanol into acetic acid.
  • Temperature influences microbial growth and the rate of fermentation. Each yeast and acetic acid
  • bacterial culture has a suitable temperature range, and excessive heat may inhibit or damage the
  • microorganisms. Therefore, temperature must be controlled according to the culture and
  • production method.
  • Acidity increases as acetic acid accumulates. The acid concentration affects microbial activity
  • and the progress of fermentation. Appropriate acidity and ethanol levels must be maintained to
  • support the desired process without inhibiting the microorganisms prematurely.
  • Oxygen supply is essential during acetic acid fermentation because acetic acid bacteria require
  • oxygen to oxidize ethanol into acetic acid. Adequate aeration supports efficient production
  • whereas insufficient oxygen can slow the process. However, excessive aeration may increase
  • evaporation and create other operational difficulties.
  • Microbial activity depends on the type, quantity and condition of the yeast and acetic acid
  • bacteria. Suitable cultures, hygienic equipment and the prevention of contamination help ensure
  • consistent fermentation. The availability of ethanol, nutrients and suitable pH also influences
  • microbial performance.
  • Other factors include the quality of the starting material, alcohol concentration, fermentation
  • time, aeration method and sanitation. After fermentation reaches the desired acidity, the vinegar
  • is clarified or filtered as required and packaged hygienically. Proper control of these factors
  • helps produce vinegar with consistent acidity, flavour, quality and keeping properties.
questions.final_answer: helps produce vinegar with consistent acidity, flavour, quality and keeping properties
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

  • storage at the appropriate temperature and relative humidity reduces moisture loss and delays
  • ripening. However, chilling-sensitive commodities must be stored within their recommended
  • temperature range. Suitable packaging protects produce from mechanical damage and reduces
  • moisture loss. Refrigerated or well-managed transportation helps maintain the cold chain and
  • prevents rapid quality deterioration.
  • Other methods include controlled atmosphere storage, modified atmosphere packaging and
  • edible coatings, which can help slow respiration and moisture loss when properly applied.
  • Sanitation, pest control and hygienic handling reduce microbial spoilage. Processing methods
  • such as canning, freezing, drying, fermentation and preparation of jams and juices convert
  • surplus or perishable produce into more stable products. Training handlers, improving storage
  • infrastructure and maintaining accurate stock rotation further reduce losses. An integrated
  • approach is most effective because post-harvest deterioration can occur at every stage between
  • harvesting and consumption.

questions.question: Discusss the factors affecting vinegar production, including temperature,acidity,oxygen supply and microbial activity
questions.solution_html:
• supply and microbial activity.
  • Vinegar is produced mainly through the conversion of ethanol into acetic acid by acetic acid
  • bacteria under aerobic conditions. The process generally involves two stages: alcoholic
  • fermentation, in which yeast converts sugars into ethanol, followed by acetic acid fermentation
  • in which suitable bacteria convert ethanol into acetic acid.
  • Temperature influences microbial growth and the rate of fermentation. Each yeast and acetic acid
  • bacterial culture has a suitable temperature range, and excessive heat may inhibit or damage the
  • microorganisms. Therefore, temperature must be controlled according to the culture and
  • production method.
  • Acidity increases as acetic acid accumulates. The acid concentration affects microbial activity
  • and the progress of fermentation. Appropriate acidity and ethanol levels must be maintained to
  • support the desired process without inhibiting the microorganisms prematurely.
  • Oxygen supply is essential during acetic acid fermentation because acetic acid bacteria require
  • oxygen to oxidize ethanol into acetic acid. Adequate aeration supports efficient production
  • whereas insufficient oxygen can slow the process. However, excessive aeration may increase
  • evaporation and create other operational difficulties.
  • Microbial activity depends on the type, quantity and condition of the yeast and acetic acid
  • bacteria. Suitable cultures, hygienic equipment and the prevention of contamination help ensure
  • consistent fermentation. The availability of ethanol, nutrients and suitable pH also influences
  • microbial performance.
  • Other factors include the quality of the starting material, alcohol concentration, fermentation
  • time, aeration method and sanitation. After fermentation reaches the desired acidity, the vinegar
  • is clarified or filtered as required and packaged hygienically. Proper control of these factors
  • helps produce vinegar with consistent acidity, flavour, quality and keeping properties.
questions.final_answer: helps produce vinegar with consistent acidity, flavour, quality and keeping properties
